metadata.name: Obesity
metadata.severity: Graded by BMI and complications; a driver of many diseases

overview.short_description: A chronic, relapsing disease of excess body fat that impairs health, defined in adults by BMI >=30 kg/m2, and a major driver of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, sleep apnoea and other conditions.
overview.detailed_description: Obesity is a common, complex chronic condition arising from an interaction of genetics, environment and behaviour. It is assessed by BMI plus waist circumference and complication burden, and managed long-term with lifestyle change, structured weight-management programmes, pharmacotherapy (including newer incretin-based agents), and bariatric surgery for selected patients. It should be addressed non-judgementally as a medical condition.
overview.pathophysiology: Chronic positive energy balance (intake exceeding expenditure) with complex neuroendocrine regulation (leptin, ghrelin, gut hormones) promotes fat accumulation. Adipose tissue is metabolically active, causing insulin resistance and chronic low-grade inflammation.
overview.etiology: Multifactorial: genetic predisposition, obesogenic environment (energy-dense diets, inactivity), socioeconomic factors, medications (steroids, some antipsychotics/antidepressants, insulin/sulfonylureas), endocrine causes (hypothyroidism, Cushing - uncommon), and monogenic/syndromic causes (rare).
overview.natural_history: Tends to be progressive and relapsing without sustained intervention; weight regain after loss is common due to physiological adaptations.
overview.prognosis: Modest sustained weight loss (5-10%) markedly improves metabolic risk; bariatric surgery can produce large, durable loss and remission of comorbidities.

prevalence.value: Very common and rising globally; a large and increasing proportion of adults and children are affected (WHO).

incidence.value: Rising worldwide with dietary and activity transitions.

mortality.value: Contributes substantially to premature death via cardiovascular disease, diabetes and cancer.

epidemiology.age_groups: All ages; childhood obesity tracks into adulthood.
epidemiology.geographic_distribution: Worldwide; high and rising in MENA and many regions.

risk_factors.lifestyle: Energy-dense diet, sugary drinks, physical inactivity, poor sleep, sedentary occupations.
risk_factors.smoking: Cessation may cause modest weight gain (not a reason to continue smoking).
risk_factors.pregnancy: Pregnancy-related weight retention; gestational diabetes risk.
risk_factors.genetic_factors: Polygenic; rare monogenic (e.g., MC4R) and syndromic (Prader-Willi) forms.
risk_factors.medications: Corticosteroids, some antipsychotics/antidepressants, insulin, sulfonylureas, certain anticonvulsants.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Hypothyroidism, Cushing syndrome (uncommon secondary causes); psychological factors/eating disorders.

chief_complaints.complaint: Concern about weight / difficulty losing weight
Complication-related symptoms (breathlessness, joint pain, snoring, low mood)
Found during review of other conditions

symptoms.symptom: Low mood, low self-esteem, or disordered eating

negative_findings.finding: No features of a secondary cause (e.g., hypothyroid symptoms, Cushingoid features)
negative_findings.why_important: Supports primary obesity rather than an endocrine cause

negative_findings.finding: No rapid unexplained weight change or red-flag symptoms
negative_findings.why_important: Argues against secondary pathology (e.g., malignancy, endocrine)

history_questions.question: How has weight changed over time and what have you tried?
history_questions.why_ask: Trajectory and prior interventions guide the plan

history_questions.question: Diet pattern, physical activity, sleep, alcohol, and eating behaviours (binge/comfort eating)?
history_questions.why_ask: Identifies modifiable drivers and disordered eating

history_questions.question: Any symptoms of hypothyroidism, Cushing's, or medications that cause weight gain?
Complications: diabetes, hypertension, joint pain, fertility/PCOS, mood?

physical_examination.examination: Signs of secondary cause (thyroid, Cushingoid features, acanthosis nigricans)
physical_examination.expected_finding: Usually absent; acanthosis suggests insulin resistance

vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: Usually normal (low in obesity hypoventilation/OSA complications)
vital_signs.bmi: >=30 kg/m2 defines obesity (>=25 overweight); ethnicity-adjusted lower thresholds for some groups

laboratory_tests.test_name: HbA1c/fasting glucose, lipid profile, blood pressure, LFTs
laboratory_tests.expected_result: May show diabetes/prediabetes, dyslipidaemia, fatty liver

laboratory_tests.test_name: TFTs (+/- cortisol testing if clinically indicated)

other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Liver biopsy only in selected NAFLD staging
other_diagnostic_tests.pcr: Genetic testing for monogenic/syndromic obesity in early-onset/severe cases
other_diagnostic_tests.sleep_study: Polysomnography/home sleep test if obstructive sleep apnoea suspected

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Adults: BMI 25-29.9 overweight; >=30 obesity (class I 30-34.9, II 35-39.9, III >=40). Interpret with waist circumference and ethnicity (lower thresholds for South Asian and some other groups) and complication burden. Children: use age/sex-specific centiles.
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_scores: BMI classification + waist circumference; complication-centred staging (e.g., Edmonton Obesity Staging System).

cutoff_values.value: BMI >=30 kg/m2 = obesity (>=27.5 in some Asian populations); waist circumference thresholds indicate central adiposity risk.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Cold intolerance, dry skin, bradycardia, raised TSH
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Do you feel cold, tired, and constipated?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Purple striae, proximal weakness, easy bruising, hypertension, diabetes
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any purple stretch marks, easy bruising, or muscle weakness?
Did weight gain start with a new medicine (steroids, antipsychotics, insulin)?
Is the weight due to swelling rather than fat?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have symptoms of an underlying cause (cold intolerance, weakness, striae) or take weight-gaining medicines?
Do you snore with daytime sleepiness, or have you developed diabetes/high blood pressure?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Positive -> targeted assessment (sleep study, metabolic work-up)

next_best_question.question: What are your main goals, eating/activity patterns, complications, and any secondary-cause features?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Primary obesity -> tiered weight-management plan (lifestyle, +/- pharmacotherapy, +/- surgery by criteria); secondary features -> investigate; complications -> manage them

next_best_test.test: Metabolic screen (HbA1c, lipids, BP, LFTs) + waist circumference

next_best_test.why: If OSA or endocrine cause suspected

red_flags.finding: Features of obstructive sleep apnoea with severe daytime sleepiness (e.g., driver)
Rapid unexplained weight gain with Cushingoid features

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Complications needing prompt care (severe OSA, obesity hypoventilation).
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Specialist/tier-3 weight management, consideration of bariatric surgery (per BMI/complication criteria), suspected endocrine cause, or complex/monogenic obesity.

initial_management.supportive_care: Compassionate, non-stigmatising approach; agree realistic goals (e.g., 5-10% loss); address drivers and comorbidities; multidisciplinary support.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide; Orlistat. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG246_2026.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Sustainable dietary change (calorie deficit, quality of diet), increased physical activity, behavioural support, sleep and stress management.
initial_management.follow_up: Regular review of weight, complications and adherence; long-term support given the relapsing nature.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Consider pharmacotherapy alongside lifestyle for eligible patients: GLP-1 receptor agonists (e.g., semaglutide, liraglutide) and dual agonists (e.g., tirzepatide) produce significant weight loss; orlistat as an option. Use within specialist/eligibility criteria. Bariatric/metabolic surgery for selected patients (e.g., BMI >=40, or >=35 with comorbidity - lower thresholds with type 2 diabetes) via specialist services.

patient_education.home_advice: Obesity is a long-term medical condition, not a lack of willpower. Losing even 5-10% of your weight brings real health benefits. Focus on gradual, sustainable changes to eating and activity; medicines and, for some people, surgery can help alongside these. Support and follow-up matter because weight tends to creep back without them.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: السِّمنة حالة طبية مزمنة وليست ضعفاً في الإرادة. حتى فقدان 5-10% من وزنك يمنح فوائد صحية حقيقية. ركّز على تغييرات تدريجية ومستدامة في الأكل والنشاط؛ وقد تساعد الأدوية، ولبعض الناس الجراحة، إلى جانب ذلك. الدعم والمتابعة مهمّان لأن الوزن يميل للعودة بدونهما.
patient_education.prevention: Healthy eating, regular activity, limiting sugary drinks, adequate sleep; early support for weight gain.
patient_education.warning_signs: Severe daytime sleepiness (unsafe driving), breathlessness/drowsiness, or features suggesting a hormonal cause.

prevention.lifestyle: Population and individual measures: healthy diet, activity, limiting sugary drinks, sleep.
prevention.screening: Opportunistic BMI/waist measurement; identify and support at-risk individuals.

evidence.evidence_level: High for lifestyle, incretin-based pharmacotherapy, and bariatric surgery outcomes.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG246_2026; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE NG246, WHO, specialist obesity guidelines.

The evidence audit verifies traceability and major safety structure; it does not certify every narrative sentence.
No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Provide non-stigmatising, long-term weight and comorbidity management.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide; Orlistat. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG246_2026.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Person-centred nutrition, activity, behavioural and psychological support; address weight-promoting medicines and sleep.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Only under current indication, BMI/comorbidity and service criteria
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: prior pancreatitis, severe gastroparesis, gallbladder disease, dehydration risk, or concurrent insulin/sulfonylurea
monitoring: weight, glucose, gastrointestinal tolerance, hydration and symptoms of pancreatitis/gallbladder disease

medication_options.when_to_consider: Eligible patient who accepts gastrointestinal effects and has no malabsorption/cholestasis
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: warfarin, ciclosporin, antiepileptics, levothyroxine, kidney-stone risk, or fat-soluble vitamin deficiency
monitoring: weight, gastrointestinal effects, interacting-drug levels and fat-soluble vitamins when prolonged

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Specialist weight service/bariatric assessment under current BMI/comorbidity criteria; urgent evaluation for eating disorder or endocrine red flags.
treatment_guidance.localization_note: Before use in Libya, align choices with the Libyan formulary, local availability, antimicrobial resistance, referral pathways and prescribing law.
